description: CalWORKs provides cash aid and related services to eligible California families. County welfare departments administer applications and ongoing cases.
introduction: CalWORKs provides cash aid and related services to eligible California families. County welfare departments administer applications and ongoing cases.

sections.who: Eligibility considers family circumstances, income and other rules. The state describes children lacking parental support because of absence, disability or death, qualifying unemployed-parent families and certain caretaker relatives.
sections.get: Monthly cash aid depends on the eligible family members, income and special needs. Families with immediate needs should ask the county about short-term assistance.
sections.docs: Prepare caregiver and child information, household income and the county’s requested evidence. Explain housing instability, childcare needs or health barriers during screening.
sections.apply:
1. Apply at BenefitsCal or a social-services office in your county.

  2. Complete the county interview and verification requests. Discuss Welfare-to-Work participation and any exemptions or good-cause circumstances.
sections.after: Follow reporting, activity and renewal notices. The state describes a 60-month adult time limit with specified exemptions. Ask about childcare and other supportive services for required activities.
sections.sources:
Application and program details: CalWORKs eligibility and application, Welfare-to-Work and time-limit guidance.

Historical screenshots and background: USA Assistance. Screenshots may show an earlier application interface.

faqs: Does every family receive the same amount?
No. Income, eligible members and other circumstances affect cash aid.
Are all adults required to do the same work activities?
No. Requirements and exemptions depend on the case.
Can the program help with an urgent need?
Ask the county about immediate short-term help and relevant services.
